questions.explanation: Scene s1: speed = distance / time = 100 / 20 = 5 metres per second.
questions.prompt: An athlete sprints 100 metres in 20 seconds. Calculate her speed.

choices.text: Correct - a flat line always means zero velocity
Wrong - the object is speeding up the whole time
Wrong - the velocity stays constant at 12 m/s, so the object keeps moving
Wrong - a flat line means the object is going backwards

questions.explanation: The trap is: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped. Flat reads as "nothing is happening", so the line feels like zero movement. The height of the line is the velocity: flat at 12 m/s means the velocity never changes, so the object keeps moving at the same speed.
questions.misconception: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped.
questions.prompt: A velocity-time graph runs flat at 12 m/s for ten seconds. A classmate says the object has stopped. Which statement is correct?

questions.explanation: Scene s2: on a distance-time graph the gradient is the speed - rise over run is 120 over 60, which is 2 metres per second.
questions.prompt: A distance-time graph climbs 120 metres in 60 seconds in a straight line. What is the speed, and how does the graph show it?

questions.explanation: Scene s3: acceleration is the gradient of a velocity-time graph - 20 over 10, which is 2 metres per second squared.
questions.prompt: A velocity-time graph rises from 0 to 20 m/s in 10 seconds. What is the acceleration?

questions.explanation: Scene s4: distance is 800 metres, so speed is 800 / 100 = 8 metres per second - but displacement is zero, so velocity is zero.
questions.prompt: A runner jogs 400 metres down a track, turns, and jogs back to the start in 100 seconds total. Find the average speed and the average velocity.
